Digital design is both communication and preparation for fabrication. Students learn how images are represented, construct clean vector geometry, communicate identity and hierarchy, animate an idea, explore artistic 3D work, and test a small interface before those skills become engraving artwork, printed parts or screen-based media.

## Learning sequence

<ol class="ter-lesson-sequence">
  <li><a href="01-raster-vector-svg.qmd">Raster, Vector &amp; SVG</a> — pixels, resolution, paths, fill, stroke, scale, and file choices.</li>
  <li><a href="02-vector-geometry.qmd">Vector Geometry &amp; Exact Construction</a> — shapes, nodes, Boolean operations, alignment, duplication, and dimensions.</li>
  <li><a href="03-logos-lettermarks.qmd">Logos, Lettermarks &amp; Negative Space</a> — identity, simplification, typography, and one-colour testing.</li>
  <li><a href="04-layout-typography-colour.qmd">Layout, Typography &amp; Colour</a> — hierarchy, spacing, contrast, readable type, and intentional palettes.</li>
  <li><a href="05-animation-ui-ux.qmd">2D Animation with Pencil2D</a> — frames, keyframes, timing, timeline, onion skinning, loops and export.</li>
  <li><a href="06-blender-artistic-3d.qmd">Blender for Artistic 3D Design</a> — mesh editing, sculptural forms, materials, lighting, rendering and animation.</li>
  <li><a href="07-website-ui-ux.qmd">Small Website &amp; UI/UX Portfolio</a> — audience, hierarchy, navigation, states, responsive layouts, files and publishing.</li>
</ol>

## Readiness for fabrication

Before moving into laser cutting, students should be able to distinguish raster engraving from vector cutting, verify document units, construct rather than trace simple geometry, remove accidental overlaps, and check a known dimension after export.

::: {.ter-project-brief}
### Suggested bridge project

Create an original logo or lettermark as a thread across later work. Test it in black and white, animate it in a 2–4 second loop, use it on a small portfolio page, engrave it on the teacher-supplied name-tag blank, or rebuild its essential geometry for the faux-enamel print.
:::

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** Strongly relevant to **TGJ2O Communications Technology**, **TDJ2O Technological Design**, and **TIJ1O Exploring Technologies**. Individual lessons support senior communications and technological-design courses involving graphic communication, digital imagery, animation, web design, interactive media, CAD, and design documentation.
:::
